name: Chapter 1: The Living World
description: Diversity, nomenclature, binomial names, taxonomy and the taxonomic hierarchy

cards.term: Which biologist has been called 'the Darwin of the 20th century'?
cards.definition: Ernst Mayr (1904–2004)

cards.term: Which definition did Ernst Mayr pioneer?
cards.definition: The currently accepted definition of a biological species

cards.term: Which central question of evolutionary biology did Mayr make it what it is today?
cards.definition: The origin of species diversity

cards.term: How many species are known and described?
cards.definition: 1.7–1.8 million

cards.term: What does each different kind of plant, animal or organism represent?
cards.definition: A species

cards.term: What does biodiversity refer to?
cards.definition: The number and types of organisms present on earth

cards.term: Why do we need scientific names instead of local names?
cards.definition: Local names vary from place to place, even within a country; a standard name is known all over the world

cards.term: What is nomenclature?
cards.definition: Standardising the naming of living organisms, so an organism has the same name all over the world

cards.term: What is identification?
cards.definition: Describing the organism correctly, so we know to which organism a name is attached

cards.term: Why must identification come before nomenclature?
cards.definition: A name can only be given once we know which organism it is attached to

cards.text: Scientific names of plants follow the {{c1::International Code for Botanical Nomenclature (ICBN)}}; animals follow the {{c2::International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN)}}.

cards.term: What three things do scientific names ensure?
cards.definition:
• Each organism has only one name
  • People anywhere can arrive at the same name
  • The name is not used for any other known organism

cards.term: What is binomial nomenclature?
cards.definition: Naming with two components: the generic name and the specific epithet

cards.term: Who gave the binomial system of nomenclature?
cards.definition: Carolus Linnaeus

cards.term: What is the scientific name of mango?
cards.definition: Mangifera indica

cards.text: In Mangifera indica, Mangifera is the {{c1::genus}} and indica is the {{c2::specific epithet}}.

cards.term: Parts of Mangifera indica Linn.
cards.definition: Mangifera = genus (capital letter); indica = specific epithet (small letter); Linn. = author (abbreviated). Italics in print, each word underlined separately in handwriting.

cards.term: In what language are biological names written?
cards.definition: Latin (Latinised or derived from Latin, whatever their origin)

cards.term: How is a biological name shown when printed, and when handwritten?
cards.definition: Printed in italics; handwritten, each word is separately underlined

cards.term: Which word of a biological name starts with a capital letter?
cards.definition: The genus. The specific epithet starts with a small letter.

cards.term: Where is the author's name written in a biological name, and how?
cards.definition: After the specific epithet, at the end, in an abbreviated form

cards.term: What does 'Linn.' in Mangifera indica Linn. tell you?
cards.definition: The species was first described by Linnaeus

cards.term: Which is written correctly: Mangifera Indica or Mangifera indica?
cards.definition: Mangifera indica: the specific epithet starts with a small letter

cards.term: What is classification?
cards.definition: Grouping anything into convenient categories based on some easily observable characters

cards.term: What is the scientific term for categories such as 'plants', 'mammals', 'dogs' and 'wheat'?
cards.definition: Taxa (singular: taxon)

cards.term: 'Animals', 'mammals' and 'dogs' are all taxa. How do they differ?
cards.definition: They are taxa at different levels: a dog is a mammal, and mammals are animals

cards.term: What is taxonomy?
cards.definition: The process of classifying all living organisms into taxa based on their characteristics

cards.term: What forms the basis of modern taxonomic studies?
cards.definition:
• External and internal structure
  • Structure of the cell
  • Development process
  • Ecological information

cards.text: The four processes basic to taxonomy are {{c1::characterisation}}, {{c2::identification}}, {{c3::classification}} and {{c4::nomenclature}}.

cards.term: On what were the earliest classifications based?
cards.definition: The 'uses' of organisms, for food, clothing and shelter

cards.term: What is systematics?
cards.definition: The study of the kinds and diversity of organisms and the relationships among them

cards.term: From which word is 'systematics' derived, and what does it mean?
cards.definition: Latin 'systema': systematic arrangement of organisms

cards.term: What was the title of the publication of Linnaeus?
cards.definition: Systema Naturae

cards.term: The scope of systematics was later enlarged to include what?
cards.definition: Identification, nomenclature and classification

cards.term: What kind of relationships does systematics take into account?
cards.definition: Evolutionary relationships between organisms

cards.term: Name four areas where taxonomic studies are useful.
cards.definition: Agriculture, forestry, industry, and knowing our bio-resources and their diversity

cards.term: Is classification a single step?
cards.definition: No. It is a hierarchy of steps, each step a rank or category

cards.text: Each step of classification is a {{c1::taxonomic category}}; all the categories together form the {{c2::taxonomic hierarchy}}.

cards.term: What is a taxon?
cards.definition: A category or rank, used as a unit of classification

cards.term: What common feature makes insects a recognisable group?
cards.definition: Three pairs of jointed legs

cards.term: Are taxonomic categories merely morphological aggregates?
cards.definition: No. They are distinct biological entities

cards.term: What is the lowest taxonomic category of all organisms?
cards.definition: Species

cards.term: What is the basic requirement for placing an organism in the various categories?
cards.definition: Knowledge of its characters

cards.term: In plants, which category takes the place of phylum?
cards.definition: Division

cards.term: Figure 1.1 · Taxonomic categories in ascending order

Which sequence of categories is correct?
(a) Species, Order, Phylum, Kingdom
(b) Genus, Species, Order, Kingdom
(c) Species, Genus, Order, Phylum
cards.definition: (a) and (c) both run upwards correctly; (b) is wrong: species comes below genus

cards.term: What is a species, taxonomically?
cards.definition: A group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities

cards.term: How is one species told apart from a closely related species?
cards.definition: By distinct morphological differences

cards.text: In Mangifera indica, Solanum tuberosum and Panthera leo, the specific epithets are {{c1::indica, tuberosum and leo}}.

cards.term: What is Solanum tuberosum?
cards.definition: Potato

cards.term: Name another species of Panthera besides leo.
cards.definition: tigris (tiger)

cards.term: Name two other species of Solanum besides tuberosum.
cards.definition: nigrum and melongena

cards.term: What is the scientific name of human beings?
cards.definition: Homo sapiens (genus Homo, species sapiens)

cards.term: What is a genus?
cards.definition: A group of related species with more characters in common than with species of other genera

cards.term: Potato and brinjal belong to which genus?
cards.definition: Solanum

cards.text: Lion ({{c1::Panthera leo}}), leopard ({{c2::P. pardus}}) and tiger ({{c3::P. tigris}}) are species of the genus Panthera.

cards.term: Which genus includes cats, and differs from Panthera?
cards.definition: Felis

cards.term: What is a family?
cards.definition: A group of related genera, with still fewer similarities than genus and species

cards.term: On what basis are plant families characterised?
cards.definition: Both vegetative and reproductive features

cards.term: Solanum, Petunia and Datura belong to which family?
cards.definition: Solanaceae

cards.term: Panthera and Felis are put together in which family?
cards.definition: Felidae

cards.term: Cats and dogs are placed in which two families?
cards.definition: Cat: Felidae. Dog: Canidae.

cards.term: What is an order?
cards.definition: An assemblage of families that show a few similar characters

cards.term: On what are order and higher categories identified?
cards.definition: Aggregates of characters

cards.term: Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are placed in which order, and on what basis?
cards.definition: Polymoniales, mainly on floral characters

cards.term: Which animal order includes the families Felidae and Canidae?
cards.definition: Carnivora

cards.term: What does the category class include?
cards.definition: Related orders

cards.term: Monkey, gorilla and gibbon belong to which order?
cards.definition: Primata

cards.term: Orders Primata and Carnivora are placed in which class?
cards.definition: Mammalia

cards.term: Fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals form which phylum?
cards.definition: Chordata

cards.term: Which common features place animals in phylum Chordata?
cards.definition: A notochord and a dorsal hollow neural system

cards.term: In plants, what are classes with a few similar characters assigned to?
cards.definition: A Division

cards.term: To which kingdom are all animals of the various phyla assigned?
cards.definition: Animalia, the highest category

cards.term: What does Kingdom Plantae comprise?
cards.definition: All plants from the various divisions

cards.term: Why have taxonomists developed sub-categories in the hierarchy?
cards.definition: For a more sound and scientific placement of the various taxa

cards.text: Going up from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics {{c1::decreases}}.

cards.term: The lower the taxon, the ___ characteristics its members share.
cards.definition: More

cards.term: Why does classification get harder at higher categories?
cards.definition: It is more difficult to determine the relationship to other taxa at the same level

cards.term: Classification of man
cards.definition: Kingdom: Animalia; Phylum / Division: Chordata; Class: Mammalia; Order: Primata; Family: Hominidae; Genus: Homo; Species: Homo sapiens
